💭My Teaching Philosophy

My teaching philosophy is based on the belief that every child deserves to learn in a safe, caring and inclusive environment where they feel valued, supported and encouraged to reach their full potential. As a future Foundation Phase teacher, I believe that teaching involves more than delivering lessons. It involves understanding learners as individuals, recognising their different abilities and creating meaningful learning experiences that support their academic, social and emotional development.

At the beginning of my teaching journey, I believed that being a good teacher mainly involved preparing interesting lessons, explaining concepts clearly and ensuring that learners understood the work. However, my practical teaching experiences have shown me that effective teaching also requires patience, flexibility, classroom management and continuous reflection.

During my Teaching Experience at Jupiter Street Primary School, I learnt that learners respond differently to teaching strategies. For example, when teaching Mathematics concepts such as fractions, I found that visual examples, questioning and interactive activities helped learners engage with the content. This strengthened my belief that young learners benefit from practical, enjoyable and learner-centred teaching experiences.

My experiences also helped me understand the importance of classroom management. Teaching Physical Education to approximately 35 Grade 3 learners showed me that even a well-planned lesson can become challenging without clear instructions, established routines and appropriate organisation. I learnt to adapt my teaching strategies to create a more structured and supportive learning environment.

I believe that positive relationships are essential for effective teaching. Learners should feel comfortable asking questions, making mistakes and expressing their ideas without fear of judgement. As a teacher, I want to encourage kindness, respect, cooperation and confidence while recognising that every learner develops at their own pace.

Reflection is another important part of my teaching philosophy. Schön (1983) highlights the importance of reflecting on professional practice. Through feedback from my mentor teacher and my own classroom experiences, I have learnt to consider what worked well, what could be improved and how I can respond more effectively to learners’ needs.

Ultimately, I want to become a teacher who inspires learners, celebrates their achievements and helps them believe in their abilities. My teaching philosophy will continue to develop as I gain experience, strengthen my knowledge and grow professionally. I believe that every child has potential, and it is my responsibility to create opportunities for that potential to flourish.

⭐My Classroom Management Approach

Classroom management plays an important role in creating a positive, organised and supportive learning environment. Throughout my Teaching Experience, I realised that effective classroom management is not simply about controlling behaviour but about establishing clear expectations, encouraging responsibility and creating an atmosphere where learners feel respected and motivated to learn.

My Classroom Management Tool: Group Reward System

During my Teaching Experience, I used a Group Reward System to encourage positive behaviour and cooperation among learners. The chart consisted of eight groups and focused on five classroom expectations.

8groups
5classroom expectations

The five expectations:

  • 👂 Listening to instructions
  • 🧼 Keeping tables clean
  • 🤝 Working as a team
  • 🙋 Raising hands
  • 💗 Showing respect

The purpose of this system was to encourage learners to take responsibility for their behaviour while working together towards shared goals. It also provided a visual reminder of the expectations within the classroom.

Theoretical Background

My classroom management approach relates to the work of three researchers and theorists:

Skinner (1953)

Operant conditioning explains how reinforcement can influence behaviour. Positive reinforcement can encourage learners to repeat desirable behaviours when their efforts are recognised.

Simonsen et al. (2008)

They emphasise the importance of evidence-based classroom management practices, including establishing clear expectations, teaching appropriate behaviour and acknowledging learners’ positive actions.

Kohn (1993)

Kohn raises concerns about relying too heavily on external rewards. This encouraged me to recognise that rewards should not be the only reason learners behave appropriately.

🌸 Learners should also develop intrinsic motivation, responsibility and respect for others.

Reflection on My Classroom Management Experience

Using the Group Reward System helped me recognise the importance of communicating expectations clearly and consistently. The system was designed to encourage teamwork and positive behaviour rather than focusing only on individual learners.

I also learnt that classroom management strategies must be fair and inclusive. Some learners may need additional support to meet expectations, and it is important that they are not discouraged or excluded because of their difficulties.

My experience teaching Physical Education also demonstrated the importance of clear instructions, established routines and organising learners into manageable groups. I realised that classroom management strategies need to be adapted according to the lesson, learning environment and learners’ needs.

Areas for Improvement

Although reward systems can support positive behaviour, I recognise the importance of gradually encouraging learners to make responsible choices without expecting rewards. In future, I would combine positive reinforcement with discussions about respect, responsibility and cooperation.

Overall, my classroom management experiences have helped me become more aware of the importance of consistency, patience and positive relationships. As a future Foundation Phase teacher, I aim to create a classroom where learners understand expectations, feel supported and develop the confidence to take responsibility for their behaviour.

🍎Reflection on My Life as a Teacher Experience

My three full days experiencing the Life of a Teacher were an important part of my final Teaching Experience at Jupiter Street Primary School. These days allowed me to gain a deeper understanding of the daily responsibilities of a teacher and helped me recognise the commitment required to manage a classroom effectively.

Before this experience, I mainly focused on preparing and presenting lessons. However, taking on the responsibilities of a teacher helped me understand that teaching involves much more than what happens during a lesson. Teachers must prepare resources, manage classroom routines, assess learners, respond to different learning needs and ensure that the classroom remains a safe and supportive environment.

One of the most valuable lessons I learnt was the importance of organisation and time management. I realised that teachers need to plan ahead while remaining flexible enough to respond to unexpected situations. Not every activity goes exactly as planned, and teachers must sometimes adjust their approach to ensure that learning continues.

Classroom management was another important part of this experience. I became more aware of the need to establish clear expectations, provide instructions and maintain learners’ attention throughout the school day. I also recognised that positive relationships with learners are essential for creating an environment where they feel comfortable, respected and motivated.

These three days challenged me to become more confident and independent in my teaching role. I learnt to take greater responsibility for my decisions and to consider how my actions could influence learners’ experiences. Although the responsibilities sometimes felt demanding, they helped me appreciate the dedication and patience required from teachers.

This experience also highlighted the importance of understanding learners as individuals. Every child has different strengths, challenges and needs. As a teacher, I must be prepared to provide encouragement, additional explanations and support where necessary.

Reflecting on these three days, I can see how much I have grown in my understanding of the teaching profession. I also recognise that I still need to strengthen my classroom management, assessment and differentiation skills.

Overall, my Life as a Teacher experience helped me develop a more realistic understanding of full-time teaching. It reinforced my passion for working with young learners and motivated me to continue developing into a responsible, caring and reflective Foundation Phase teacher.

🤲Reflection on My Service-learning Experience

🌸 Project: Nourish and Care – Foundation Phase Support Initiative

My Service-learning experience was one of the most meaningful and rewarding parts of my teaching journey. Through my Social Action Project, Nourish and Care: Foundation Phase Support Initiative, I had the opportunity to make a positive contribution to the well-being of Foundation Phase learners at Jupiter Street Primary School. The project focused on addressing food insecurity and promoting personal hygiene, aligning with Sustainable Development Goal 2: Zero Hunger and Sustainable Development Goal 6: Clean Water and Sanitation.

The project involved distributing handwashing awareness posters to Foundation Phase classrooms, organising an educational handwashing demonstration, and providing learners with toiletry packs, hot dogs and sweet treats. I invited SR Sheryl Hightree to present an interactive lesson about proper handwashing techniques, germs and cross-contamination. This was an important part of the project because it encouraged learners to develop healthy hygiene habits that they could practise in their everyday lives.

One of the greatest successes of this project was being able to combine education with practical support. The handwashing posters provided ongoing reminders about personal hygiene, while the food and toiletry distributions addressed learners’ immediate needs. I also recognised the importance of involving the wider community, as the project was made possible through sponsorships, donations and assistance from family and friends.

During the planning and implementation stages, I learned that organising a community project requires careful preparation, communication and time management. Securing sponsorships, coordinating the educational demonstration and arranging the distribution of resources required commitment and organisation. These responsibilities challenged me to become more independent, resourceful and confident in communicating with different people.

This experience taught me valuable lessons about compassion, teamwork, leadership and social responsibility. I realised that teachers have responsibilities extending beyond delivering lessons and assessing academic progress. Learners’ personal circumstances, including access to food and hygiene products, can influence their well-being and ability to participate meaningfully in learning activities.

On a personal level, this project strengthened my appreciation for the importance of kindness and community involvement. Being able to contribute towards meeting learners’ needs reminded me why I chose the teaching profession. It also encouraged me to become more aware of the challenges faced by families and the importance of supporting learners without making assumptions about their circumstances.

Reflecting on this experience, I recognise that providing resources offers immediate support, while developing sustainable partnerships and reinforcing healthy habits can contribute to longer-term change. In future, I would aim to strengthen ongoing community involvement and explore ways to maintain the project’s impact.

Overall, this Service-learning experience contributed significantly to my personal and professional growth. It reinforced my belief that teaching involves nurturing the whole child and creating a caring, inclusive and supportive school environment. As a future Foundation Phase teacher, I hope to continue making a meaningful difference both inside and beyond the classroom.

💻Reflection on My Online Microteaching Experience

My Online Microteaching experience was an enjoyable and valuable part of my journey towards becoming a Foundation Phase teacher. It provided me with an opportunity to explore how technology can be used to make lessons more interactive, engaging and meaningful. For my microteaching lesson, I focused on Mathematics, specifically fractions, and incorporated visual examples, questioning and SplashLearn activities to support learning.

One of the most successful aspects of my lesson was the level of participation and engagement. The learners showed enthusiasm when completing the SplashLearn activities and were willing to answer questions and share their understanding. I used visual examples to demonstrate how fractions represent equal parts of a whole. This helped make an abstract mathematical concept easier to understand. I was pleased that most learners could identify fractions and count equal parts correctly.

Throughout the lesson, I assessed understanding through questioning, observing responses and using the interactive activities. This reminded me that assessment does not always have to involve formal written tasks. Asking questions and observing participation can provide valuable information about learners’ understanding and help teachers identify where additional support may be needed.

Another important lesson I learnt was the value of using different teaching strategies to accommodate diverse learning needs. By combining explanations, visual examples and interactive activities, I created opportunities for learners to engage with the content in different ways. I also recognised the importance of providing step-by-step guidance and additional challenges for learners who understand the concepts more quickly.

Although the lesson went well overall, I identified areas that I could improve. I would allow more time for independent practice, particularly when helping learners understand the difference between the numerator and denominator. I would also include additional questions to check individual understanding before moving on to another activity. This would help me identify misconceptions and provide support where necessary.

This experience strengthened my confidence in using digital resources as part of my teaching. It showed me that technology can support learning when it is carefully selected and aligned with lesson objectives. However, I also realised that technology should not simply be used to entertain learners but should contribute towards developing their knowledge and understanding.

Overall, my Online Microteaching experience encouraged me to become more creative, reflective and confident in my teaching abilities. It reinforced my belief that Foundation Phase learners benefit from practical, visual and interactive learning opportunities. As a future teacher, I hope to continue exploring meaningful ways of incorporating technology into my lessons while ensuring that every learner feels included, supported and motivated to learn.

🎓Reflection on Becoming a Professional Teacher

Completing my final Teaching Experience has been an important part of my journey towards becoming a professional teacher. Throughout my eight weeks at Jupiter Street Primary, I had the opportunity to apply what I have learnt during my Bachelor of Education studies in a real classroom environment. This experience allowed me to recognise how much I have grown, understand the responsibilities of a teacher and reflect on the areas in which I still need to develop.

Experiencing the Life of a Teacher

The three full days in the “Life of a Teacher” role gave me a better understanding of what being a full-time teacher involves. It allowed me to experience teaching beyond simply presenting lessons. I became more aware of the importance of planning ahead, managing classroom routines, preparing resources, assessing learners and ensuring that their individual needs are considered. I realised that teachers have responsibilities throughout the school day, including before and after lessons. Although these three days were challenging, they helped me appreciate the amount of time, patience and commitment required from a teacher.

Understanding the Realities of Full-Time Teaching

One of the biggest insights I gained was that teaching requires flexibility and the ability to manage several responsibilities at once. A teacher does not only focus on completing the curriculum but also plays an important role in learners’ emotional, social and academic development. Every learner is different, and some may require additional explanations, encouragement or support. I also realised that unexpected situations can occur, meaning that teachers need to adjust their plans when necessary. Full-time teaching requires organisation, communication, patience and a genuine interest in the well-being of learners. It has taught me that teaching is not simply a job but a responsibility towards the children entrusted to us.

Comparing the First Four Weeks with the Last Four Weeks

I experienced a noticeable difference between the first four weeks and the last four weeks of my Teaching Experience. During the first four weeks, I focused more on observing, planning, discussing my ideas with my mentor teacher and becoming familiar with the learners and the classroom environment. I used this time to understand the classroom routines, identify learners’ needs and prepare myself for taking on more teaching responsibilities.

During the last four weeks, I became more involved in the educational programme and took greater responsibility for planning and presenting lessons. I became more confident in front of the class and learnt how to manage the learners while delivering lessons. I also had the opportunity to participate in the social action component of my Teaching Experience. This showed me that a teacher’s responsibility extends beyond academic learning and includes contributing positively to the school community. Looking back, I can see that I became more independent and comfortable in my role.

Challenges and How I Overcame Them

One of the aspects I initially found challenging was classroom management, especially keeping learners focused while making sure that everyone understood the lesson. I also sometimes doubted myself and worried about whether my lessons would go according to plan. I addressed these challenges by preparing thoroughly, establishing clear expectations and using different teaching strategies to maintain learners’ interest. I learnt the importance of giving clear instructions, asking questions and checking learners’ understanding throughout a lesson. I also became more comfortable asking my mentor teacher for guidance and using feedback to improve. These experiences taught me that challenges are part of becoming a teacher and that confidence develops through practice and experience.

My Readiness to Enter the Teaching Profession

As a final-year B.Ed Foundation Phase student, I feel more prepared to enter the teaching profession than I did at the beginning of my studies. I feel confident in my ability to build positive relationships with learners, plan CAPS-aligned lessons and create a welcoming classroom environment where learners feel valued and included. I also believe that one of my strengths is my willingness to understand learners as individuals rather than seeing them only as learners who need to complete schoolwork.

However, I recognise that I still have areas in which I would like to grow. These include improving my classroom management, developing more effective differentiation strategies, strengthening my assessment practices and gaining further experience in supporting learners with different learning needs. I understand that becoming a good teacher is an ongoing process and that I will continue learning throughout my career.

Mentor Teacher Feedback and My Professional Growth

The guidance and feedback from my mentor teacher played an important role in my development. Having someone who could guide me with lesson planning, classroom management and teaching strategies helped me identify both my strengths and the areas that needed improvement. I learnt to accept constructive feedback positively instead of viewing it as criticism. I also became more aware of the importance of reflecting on each lesson and considering what worked well and what could be done differently.

During this final Teaching Experience, I noticed improvements in my confidence, preparation, communication and ability to adapt my teaching. I became more comfortable taking responsibility for the classroom and responding to learners’ needs. I also learnt that a successful lesson is not only about completing everything planned but about ensuring that learners understand and are actively involved in their learning.

My Strengths and Goals for Continued Professional Development

Based on my Teaching Experience, I believe my strengths as a beginner teacher include patience, empathy, commitment, creativity and building positive relationships with learners. I want to be the kind of teacher who makes every child feel seen, heard and supported. I strongly believe that every child deserves a teacher who recognises their potential and encourages them to believe in themselves, regardless of their circumstances.

Moving forward, my goals are to continue developing my teaching strategies, improve my knowledge of inclusive education, gain more experience with assessment and explore ways of using technology meaningfully in the classroom. I also want to continue learning from experienced teachers and attending professional development opportunities.

Overall, my final Teaching Experience has strengthened my decision to pursue a career in teaching. It has shown me that teaching comes with challenges, responsibilities and moments that require patience, but it is also a profession filled with opportunities to make a difference. I know that I will not enter the profession knowing everything, but I am willing to learn, grow and improve. I hope to become a teacher who not only teaches children but also inspires them, supports them and helps them recognise their own potential.

My journey as a teacher is only beginning, and I look forward to the difference I can make in the lives of my future learners.
